_comment: STAGE-D per-batch coverage registry -- batch 'circuit_ir' (D15, Tier-2 frontend cluster)
(docs/SIMULATOR.md SS12.3/12.4; full-coverage program;
work-list docs/SIMULATOR.md D15).
Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/circuit_ir.py -- the user-facing, Stim-compatible circuit IR of the simulator
frontend: five frozen dataclasses (GateOp / Tick / MeasureOp / DetectorDef / ObservableDef) whose
load-bearing __post_init__ normalizes names/targets/keys/args/coords/index; the CircuitIR container
(a big validating __post_init__ + three record-schema properties measurement_keys / detector_names /
observable_names); and the CircuitBuilder fluent API (gate/tick/h/x/y/idle/cz/cx/reset/measure/
detector/observable/declare_static_zz_couplings/declare_axis1_local_lindblad_context/build). The
module imports NEITHER torch NOR quimb (dataclasses + typing only; its axis-1 declare methods call
metadata_guard/axis1_context helpers which are numpy/math-free), so EVERY public unit is CPU-PURE and
IN-SCOPE for full L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {} (the AST reconcile refuses any gpu_bound
claim on a torch-less module).
TWENTY-THREE public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every public
method of a top-level class + the load-bearing __post_init__ dunder of each frozen dataclass). Tick has
NO __post_init__ (body is a docstring) so it contributes no unit; CircuitBuilder.__init__ and the
_validate_targets/_require_known_keys private methods are NOT units (covered via the public paths).
The four module-level helpers (_as_targets/_as_args/_validate_targets/_require_known_keys) are private
-> not reconciled/scored, but ARE exercised + mutation-covered through the public builder/CircuitIR
paths (mutmut is coverage-guided). The unit set:
* 5 dataclass __post_init__: GateOp / MeasureOp / DetectorDef / ObservableDef / CircuitIR.
* 3 CircuitIR properties: measurement_keys / detector_names / observable_names.
* 15 CircuitBuilder methods: gate / tick / h / x / y / idle / cz / cx / reset / measure / detector /
observable / declare_static_zz_couplings / declare_axis1_local_lindblad_context / build.
CPU discipline. Every unit runs on plain-Python dataclass construction (no Stim, no simulator run), so
the tests are fast + deterministic. The workhorse is EXACT-STRUCTURE pinning: a from-scratch _view()
reconstruction of each step's (kind,name,targets,keys/coords/args/index) tuple pins the built CircuitIR
ordered steps against an INDEPENDENT expectation (NOT the module's own accessors). The record-schema
properties (measurement_keys/detector_names/observable_names) are pinned vs an INDEPENDENT extraction
from the constructed steps (a comprehension over the step tuples the test built, NOT the module's
property), with an assert_discriminates variant carrying a dropped/wrong name. Every validation RAISE
asserts its EXACT message via str(excinfo.value)==... so mutmut string-literal wrap/case mutants die
(a substring match= lets them survive but exact-equality kills them).
SET-ELEMENT string mutants: the module-level _RECORD_AFFECTING_GATE_NAMES + _SOURCE_NOISE_GATE_NAMES
sets are killed by PARAMETRIZED coverage of EVERY element -- each name is fed as a GateOp inside a
CircuitIR and must raise its dedicated ValueError (removing/mutating any set element makes that name no
longer trip the guard, so the per-element raise assertion fails -> mutant killed). The source-noise
allow path (_allow_noise_steps InitVar True) is exercised too (bool() coercion + the `not allow` False
arc). Both _validate_targets arcs (t<0 and t>=num_qubits) and both _require_known_keys arcs (missing
vs present) are tripped through the CircuitIR + builder routes.
NO exemptions + NO out_of_scope: every guard is REACHABLE through a constructor/builder route (checked,
not assumed -- the D13 default-arg/guard-route lesson): the num_qubits<=0 guard (CircuitIR + builder),
every record-affecting/source-noise GateOp raise, the measurement-key mismatch + duplicate-key raises,
the duplicate-detector-name / unknown-key / observable-index-negative / duplicate-observable-index
raises, the unknown-step TypeError, the metadata reserved-key raise (pinned with its CircuitIR.metadata
label), the CZ/CX even-length guard, the measure basis/reset name map + invalid-basis raise, and the
declare_* metadata set-vs-pop branches (the calibrations else-pop is exercised BOTH on an absent key
-- so the pop's default-None arg is load-bearing -- AND on a present key that the second call removes).
